PCA_STRUCT

Alex Depew

2026-02-04

File information

This script is used to evaluate temporal patterns in population structure in all wood bison herds in Canada.

Files used described below:

  • Cleaned_samples.06.01.2026.csv
    • Contains all samples for population genetic analyses, post-filtering

Load Required Packages

rm(list = ls())
library(adegenet)
## Loading required package: ade4
## 
##    /// adegenet 2.1.11 is loaded ////////////
## 
##    > overview: '?adegenet'
##    > tutorials/doc/questions: 'adegenetWeb()' 
##    > bug reports/feature requests: adegenetIssues()
library(graph4lg)
## Welcome to 'graph4lg' package. Let's do landscape genetics analysis with graphs
library(poppr)
## Registered S3 method overwritten by 'pegas':
##   method      from
##   print.amova ade4
## This is poppr version 2.9.8. To get started, type package?poppr
## OMP parallel support: available
library(hierfstat)
## 
## Attaching package: 'hierfstat'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:adegenet':
## 
##     Hs, read.fstat
library(pophelper)
## pophelper v2.3.1 ready.
library(dplyr)
##

## The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':

## The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
## 
##     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

Load Required Data

bison.data <- read.csv("Cleaned_samples.06.01.2026.csv",
                       check.names = F)

Convert data to Genind object

# Make genind object
bison.genind <- df2genind(X=bison.data[,c(19:ncol(bison.data))],
                              sep = "/",
                              ind.names = bison.data$Spreadsheet_ID,
                              loc.names = NULL,
                              pop = bison.data$HERD,
                              NA.char = "NA",
                              ploidy = 2,
                              type = "codom",
                              strata = NULL,
                              hierarchy = NULL)

# Attach collection year metadata
idx <- match(indNames(bison.genind), bison.data$Spreadsheet_ID)
stopifnot(!any(is.na(idx)))
bison.genind@other$YEAR.ASSIGN <- bison.data$YEAR.ASSIGN[idx]

# Remove loci with more than 20% missing data
bison.genind <- missingno(bison.genind, type = "loci", cutoff = 0.20)
## 
## Found 2945 missing values.
## 
## 1 locus contained missing values greater than 20%
## 
## Removing 1 locus: , BM4028

Subset data

Data is subset into three temporal groups. Temporal groups are: 1: pre-1999, 2: pre-2016, and 3: post-2016

# Create datasets containing samples of interest for temporal comparisons
temp1 <- bison.genind[bison.genind@other$YEAR.ASSIGN <=1999,]
temp1.sum <- summary(temp1) # Create summary of genind object

temp2 <- bison.genind[bison.genind@other$YEAR.ASSIGN >= 2000 & bison.genind@other$YEAR.ASSIGN <= 2015, ]
temp2.sum <- summary(temp2)

temp3 <- bison.genind[bison.genind@other$YEAR.ASSIGN >=2016,]
temp3.sum <- summary(temp3)


# Remove populations which do not contain significant sample sizes in temporal groups
table(pop(temp1))
## 
##  WBNPGR WBNPPAD  WBNPNY  WBNPLB  WBNPHC   EINPP   EINPW     MBS 
##      10      24      13      11      23      30      39      28
table(pop(temp2)) # WBNP samples, ETH, NORD samples can be removed
## 
##     ETH      HZ      RL     WAB WBNPPAD  WBNPNY   EINPP   EINPW     MBS    NORD 
##       6      33      19      10       1       5      32      40      51       5 
##    WENT 
##       5
table(pop(temp3))
## 
##      CL     ETH      HZ     NAH      RL     WAB    WBNP  WBNPGR WBNPPAD  WBNPNY 
##      20      31      20       8      29       8      67      21      34      32 
##  WBNPLB  WBNPHC   EINPP   EINPW    NORD    WENT    AISH 
##      25      30      35      19      17       4      63
# Remove herds from temporal group 2 and 3
remove_herds <- c("WBNPPAD", "WBNPNY", "ETH", "NORD", "WENT")
temp2 <- temp2[!pop(temp2) %in% remove_herds, ]
temp2.sum <- summary(temp2) # Recalculate summary

temp3 <- temp3[!pop(temp3) %in% "WBNP"]
temp3.sum <- summary(temp3) # Recalculate summary

Remove Elk Island Plains for Structure Analyses

temp1 <- temp1[temp1@pop != "EINPP"]
temp1.sum <- summary(temp1)

temp2 <- temp2[temp2@pop != "EINPP"]
temp2.sum <- summary(temp2)

temp3 <- temp3[temp3@pop != "EINPP"]
temp3.sum <- summary(temp3)

Principal Coordinate Analysis (PCA)

Visualize population structure without assumptions of HWE or LD, to identify clusters in the data.

Temporal Group 1

x.temp1 <- tab(temp1, freq = TRUE, NA.method = "mean")
pca.temp1 <- dudi.pca(x.temp1, center = T, scale = F, scannf = F, nf = 2)


s.class(pca.temp1$li, fac = pop(temp1), col = transp(funky(15)),
        axesell = F, cstar = 0, cpoint = 3,
        grid = F)

# How much % variance do the axes represent?
eig.perc.temp1 <- 100*pca.temp1$eig/sum(pca.temp1$eig)
head(eig.perc.temp1)
## [1] 5.204101 3.078503 3.029042 2.859461 2.722830 2.469633
# Allele contributions to variance
loadingplot(pca.temp1$c1^2)

### Temporal Group 2

x.temp2 <- tab(temp2, freq = TRUE, NA.method = "mean")
pca.temp2 <- dudi.pca(x.temp2, center = T, scale = F, scannf = F, nf = 2)


s.class(pca.temp2$li, fac = pop(temp2), col = transp(funky(15)),
        axesell = F, cstar = 0, cpoint = 3,
        grid = F)

# How much % variance do the axes represent?
eig.perc.temp2 <- 100*pca.temp2$eig/sum(pca.temp2$eig)
head(eig.perc.temp2)
## [1] 6.812642 5.203684 4.605199 3.020669 2.861094 2.546459
# Allele contributions to variance
loadingplot(pca.temp2$c1^2)

### Temporal Group 3

x.temp3 <- tab(temp3, freq = TRUE, NA.method = "mean")
pca.temp3 <- dudi.pca(x.temp3, center = T, scale = F, scannf = F, nf = 2)


s.class(pca.temp3$li, fac = pop(temp3), col = transp(funky(15)),
        axesell = F, cstar = 0, cpoint = 3,
        grid = F)

# How much % variance do the axes represent?
eig.perc.temp3 <- 100*pca.temp3$eig/sum(pca.temp3$eig)
head(eig.perc.temp3)
## [1] 5.012402 3.456243 2.896918 2.363685 2.156868 2.133474
# Allele contributions to variance
loadingplot(pca.temp3$c1^2)

STRUCTURE VISUALIZATION

Subset csv

The data csv file can be subset to match the samples included in each STRUCTURE run. This will be used to match the sample ID’s for plotting on the STRUCTURE plot.

temp1.data <- bison.data %>%
  select(-ID) %>% 
  filter(YEAR.ASSIGN <= 1999) %>%
  rename(ID = Spreadsheet_ID) %>%     
  mutate(ID = as.character(ID)) %>% 
  filter(HERD != "EINPP")

temp2.data <- bison.data %>% 
  select(-ID) %>% 
  filter(YEAR.ASSIGN >=2000 &
           YEAR.ASSIGN <=2015) %>%
  filter(!HERD %in% remove_herds) %>%
  rename(ID = Spreadsheet_ID) %>% 
  mutate(ID = as.character(ID)) %>% 
  filter(HERD != "EINPP")

  
temp3.data <- temp2.data <- bison.data %>% 
  select(-ID) %>%
  filter(YEAR.ASSIGN >=2016) %>%
  filter(HERD != "WBNP") %>% 
  rename(ID = Spreadsheet_ID) %>% 
  mutate(ID = as.character(ID)) %>% 
  filter(HERD != "EINPP")

Temporal Group 1

Load Data

sfiles_temp1 <- list.files("C:/Users/User/Documents/R_WD/woodbison/structure/STRUCTURE_RESULTS/temp1/", full.names = TRUE)
slist_temp1 <- readQ(files = sfiles_temp1, filetype = "structure")

Optimal K clusters

struct_sum_temp1 <- summariseQ(tabulateQ(slist_temp1))

p1 <- evannoMethodStructure(data = struct_sum_temp1, exportplot = F,
                           returnplot = T, returndata = F,
                           basesize = 12, linesize = 0.7)

Plotting

ind_label_temp1 <- rownames_to_column(ind_label_temp1, "ID")

locations_temp1 <- left_join(ind_label_temp1, temp1.data, by = "ID")

Temporal Group 2

Load Data

sfiles_temp2 <- list.files("C:/Users/User/Documents/R_WD/woodbison/structure/STRUCTURE_RESULTS/temp2", full.names = TRUE)
slist_temp2 <- readQ(files = sfiles_temp2, filetype = "structure")

Optimal K clusters

struct_sum_temp2 <- summariseQ(tabulateQ(slist_temp2))

p2 <- evannoMethodStructure(data = struct_sum_temp2, exportplot = F,
                           returnplot = T, returndata = F,
                           basesize = 12, linesize = 0.7)
grid.arrange(p2)

Plotting

# Organize into individual and population order
ind_label_temp2 <- readQ(files = sfiles_temp2[1], indlabfrom = TRUE) %>% as.data.frame()
ind_label_temp2 <- rownames_to_column(ind_label_temp2, "ID")

locations_temp2 <- left_join(ind_label_temp2, temp2.data, by = "ID")

slist <- slist_temp2

temp2_ind_order <- locations_temp2
rownames(slist[[1]]) <- temp2_ind_order$ID
if(length(unique(sapply(slist,nrow)))==1) slist <- lapply(slist,"rownames<-",temp2_ind_order$ID)
lapply(slist, rownames)[0:50]

Temporal Group 3

Load Data

sfiles_temp3 <- list.files("C:/Users/User/Documents/R_WD/woodbison/structure/STRUCTURE_RESULTS/temp3/", full.names = TRUE)
slist_temp3 <- readQ(files = sfiles_temp3, filetype = "structure")

Optimal K clusters

struct_sum_temp3 <- summariseQ(tabulateQ(slist_temp3))

p3 <- evannoMethodStructure(data = struct_sum_temp3, exportplot = F,
                           returnplot = T, returndata = F,
                           basesize = 12, linesize = 0.7)
grid.arrange(p3)

# Organize into individual and population order
ind_label_temp3 <- readQ(files = sfiles_temp3[1], indlabfrom = TRUE) %>% as.data.frame()
ind_label_temp3 <- rownames_to_column(ind_label_temp3, "ID")

locations_temp3 <- left_join(ind_label_temp3, temp3.data, by = "ID")

slist <- slist_temp3

temp3_ind_order <- locations_temp3
rownames(slist[[1]]) <- temp3_ind_order$ID
if(length(unique(sapply(slist,nrow)))==1) slist <- lapply(slist,"rownames<-",temp3_ind_order$ID)
lapply(slist, rownames)[0:150]

slist_temp3 <- slist
slist_align3 <- alignK(slist_temp3, "within")

loc_labels_temp3 <- locations_temp3$HERD %>% as.data.frame()
colnames(loc_labels_temp3) <- "Region"

herd_order_temp3 <- c("AISH", "CL", "EINPW", "ETH", "HZ", "NAH", 
                      "NORD", "RL", "WAB", "WBNPGR", "WBNPHC", "WBNPLB", 
                      "WBNPNY", "WBNPPAD", "WENT")


# Structure Plot
plotQ(slist_align3[15], 
            basesize = 10, 
            clustercol = colours, 
            grplab = loc_labels_temp3, 
            subsetgrp = herd_order_temp3, 
            ordergrp = TRUE,
            showindlab = TRUE, 
            indlabsize = 4,        
            indlabangle = 90,
            indlabheight = 0,       
            grplabsize = 3, 
            grplabangle = 0,
            grplabpos = 0.65,
            grplabheight = 0.2,      
            grplabspacer = 0.1,
            linesize = 1,          
            pointsize = 4, 
            divcol = "white",
            divsize = 1, 
            useindlab = TRUE, 
            returndata = TRUE,
            height = 12,             
            width = 35,
            exportpath = "./plots/structure_plots/")
